description:
TARGET A, MEASURED: a WARM `pcl` run of a script that uses Moo with ONE `has`
costs ~5 s, every run, for ever -- and four of the modules it loads rebuild
their fasl on EVERY run instead of ever reaching a FASL HIT.

FOUND s490a (Opus), while taking #1860's warm-start A/B numbers.  Present
identically at ab4da8b4 and on the s490a tree, so it is neither caused nor
cured by that batch; filed rather than chased, per the structural-first rule.

MEASUREMENT (scratch/s490a/probes/p-moowarm2.pl in the s490a worktree; one
fresh PCL_CACHE_DIR per case, runs 2-4 are all warm, PCL_FASL_DEBUG counted):

    use Moo only    run 2: 0.88s   FASL HIT=1  TEXT=7  fasl-build=3
    use Moo only    run 3: 0.63s   FASL HIT=4  TEXT=4  fasl-build=3
    use Moo only    run 4: 0.34s   FASL HIT=7          fasl-build=4
    use Moo + has   run 2: 6.83s   FASL HIT=3  TEXT=8  fasl-build=6
    use Moo + has   run 3: 5.76s   FASL HIT=8  TEXT=4  fasl-build=4
    use Moo + has   run 4: 5.53s   FASL HIT=12         fasl-build=4

TWO SEPARATE FINDINGS IN ONE TABLE:

(a) THE FASL LADDER, and a floor it never reaches.  A module loaded through
    the TEXT path builds its fasl on a LATER run, so the cache takes three or
    four runs to settle -- and it never fully settles: at run 4 both cases
    still show `fasl-build=4`, i.e. four modules recompile every single run.
    That is a permanent per-run cost nobody has measured before.  The obvious
    suspects are the entries whose `.lisp` is valid but whose fasl build fails
    or is not kept (%p-build-module-fasl's failure path is silent), and a
    module whose source and entry land in the same second (the strictly-newer
    rule) -- discriminate by dumping which module names carry the count.

(b) ONE `has` COSTS ~5 s PER WARM RUN.  `use Moo` alone settles at 0.34 s,
    which matches the number docs/caching.md quotes (0.417 s).  Adding
    `has x => (is => 'rw')` to a package adds ~5.2 s to EVERY run, warm, with
    only 4 eval-cache entries written -- so it is not the string-eval
    transpile being repeated.  Sub::Quote builds the accessor as a code string
    and PCL then has SBCL compile it at run time, every run: the suspicion to
    kill first is "the generated accessor is COMPILEd per run, and nothing
    caches the compiled form of an eval" (the eval cache stores the CL TEXT,
    task #1200, not a fasl).  The cheap discriminating measurement: time
    `has` with PCL_NO_FASL_CACHE=1 and with the eval cache disabled, and count
    `compile` calls in the run -- three minutes, and it says whether the fix
    is an eval FASL layer or something in the accessor lowering.

WHY IT MATTERS: Target A is absolute speed, `use Moo` is the flagship
warm-start number in docs/caching.md and README, and a Moo class with one
attribute is the smallest realistic Moo program there is.  perl runs the same
script in 0.09 s.

Related: #1200 (the eval disk cache -- text, not fasl), #1188 (the module fasl
cache), #1841 (the script cache), docs/caching.md Â§5's measured table.


=== BEFORE NUMBERS + REVIEW PROBE (s491, Fable, 2026-09-19; main 4c6565e5) ===
Probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s491/probes/p1910-moo.pl (a Moo class with six `has` incl. lazy/isa/coerce/trigger, an `around`, an `extends` + `has '+step'`; .perl.out beside it).  `PCL_CACHE_DIR=<fresh, mode 700> ./pcl` on main, load ~2.8 (two agents starting, so ABSOLUTE times are high; the SHAPE is the finding): COLD 25.85 s, WARM 9.57 s, WARM-again 7.80 s, WARM-3 7.49 s -- it never settles below ~7.5 s; stdout == perl on all four runs (hit == miss == perl holds today and is the correctness bar for any fix).  stderr carries a line on every run that is NOT this task: #1917 (Class::XSAccessor "exists but failed to load").  NOTE for the measurement: a PCL_CACHE_DIR that is group-writable is REFUSED (rc 2) -- create it with mode 700.

================================================================
=== MECHANISM LOCATED (s473x, 2026-09-19, Opus; member 1b) â BOTH OF THIS
=== TASK'S HYPOTHESES ARE DEAD, AND THE ANSWER IS #1202 ===

Measured in worktree agent-a30d9e89a150f4423 on main 4c6565e5, quiet box
(1-min load 0.3â1.5), one fresh `PCL_CACHE_DIR` per case (mode 700).

(a) "THE FASL LADDER NEVER SETTLES" IS WRONG â IT SETTLES AFTER FIVE RUNS.
    This task's table stopped at run 4, which is the last run that still
    builds.  Six warm runs of `package Pt; use Moo; has x => (is=>'rw');`
    (probes/p1910b.pl, raw PCL_FASL_DEBUG kept):

        run 1  19.33 s   HIT 0   TEXT 14   build 4
        run 2   6.34 s   HIT 3   TEXT  8   build 6
        run 3   5.45 s   HIT 8   TEXT  4   build 4
        run 4   4.94 s   HIT 12  TEXT  0   build 4
        run 5   4.42 s   HIT 16  TEXT  0   build 0     <-- settled
        run 6   4.40 s   HIT 16  TEXT  0   build 0

    Every module is a FASL HIT from run 5 on; `fasl-build=4` at run 4 is the
    last rung of the ladder, not a floor.  So there is NO never-settling cache
    key and nothing to fix in the module cache.  A module whose fasl is built
    on run N is a HIT on run N+1: the ladder is one rung per run because a
    fasl is built only after its text has been loaded once.

(b) "ONE `has` COSTS ~5 s" IS RIGHT, AND IT IS NOT `compile` OF MOO ACCESSORS.
    sb-sprof :cpu over the whole warm run (probes/p1910prof.pl MODE=prof):
    the flat profile is ~100 % `sb-c::*` â join-type-constraints 8.7 %,
    constraint-propagate-in-block 4.9 %, delq1 4.8 %, conset= 3.7 %, â¦ â i.e.
    the SBCL COMPILER, at run time.  Encapsulating `sb-c::compile-in-lexenv`
    (MODE=count, and probes/p1910who.pl for the forms) says 149â195 calls and
    4.36â4.70 s, and names the three slowest:

        1.374 s  (lambda nil (let ((local-sym (%p-reserve-sub-name 'pl-_pack_tmpl)) â¦
        0.900 s  â¦ 'pl-_unpack_tmpl â¦
        0.487 s  â¦ 'pl-_unpack_str â¦

    Those are subs of `cl/pcl-pack.lisp`.  The eval disk cache is innocent: the
    run writes exactly THREE `evals/` entries (428, 2169 and 8927 bytes) and
    the biggest of them, Moo's constructor, compiles in 0.568 s.

    Encapsulating `pcl::p-load-extension` with a backtrace (probes/p1910ext.pl)
    closes it:

        EXT-LOAD-START pcl-pack
         0: (P-LOAD-EXTENSION "pcl-pack")
         1: (P-PACK "F" 0)
         2: ("top level form")   <- of ~/.pcl-cache/modules/<hash>.fasl,
                                    the CACHED FASL OF Sub/Quote.pm
         â¦
        13: (P-USE "Sub::Quote" :IMPORT-ARGS #("quote_sub" "quotify") â¦)
        EXT-LOAD-END pcl-pack 3.978 s

    **Sub::Quote's top-level code calls `pack("F",0)`, the self-loading stub
    fires, and `p-load-extension` does a plain `(load "cl/pcl-pack.lisp")` â
    so SBCL recompiles the whole checked-in pack artifact on EVERY run.**
    That is task #1202 verbatim, reached by a program that never mentions
    pack, and it is ~4.0 s of the ~4.4 s.

THE PRIZE TABLE (probes/p1202table.pl; each case its own fresh cache dir,
six warm runs to settle the ladder, then best of three; the extension column
comes from a re-run under an encapsulation of p-load-extension):

    case                  perl(s)   pcl(s)   extensions loaded
    a strict+warnings       0.004    0.042   none
    b use Moo               0.010    0.067   none
    c Moo + one has         0.014    4.389   pcl-pack 4.015 s
    d mro::get_linear_isa   0.003    0.085   pcl-mro  0.046 s
    e JSON::PP encode       0.013    0.231   none
    f pack("N",1)           0.002    3.598   pcl-pack 3.914 s
    g print "ok"            0.003    0.039   none

    So `use Moo` alone is 0.067 s once settled â the 0.34 s this task recorded
    was run 4 of the ladder, not the floor â and ONE `has` adds 4.32 s, of
    which 4.015 s is the pack extension load.  `pcl-warnings` never loads for
    `use warnings`; `pcl-mro` is real but small (46 ms).

#1917 (the "Class::XSAccessor exists but failed to load" line), A/B'd here
because it shares the run: `MOO_XS_DISABLE=1` reads 4.300 / 4.351 s at runs
5 / 6 against 4.419 / 4.401 s with the attempt â **0.05â0.12 s warm**, plus
one fewer module in the cache (XSAccessor.pm is transpiled on the cold run:
19.33 s vs 18.80 s, ~0.5 s cold).  It is ~1 % of the warm run and NOT this
task's 4 s.

STATUS: the lever is #1202's, the extension load is USER-PARKED
(plan-speed-and-ir-s470.md Â§A.0 and Â§A.2's last row), and s473x did NOT build
it â Fable put the question to the USER with these numbers.  Nothing else in
#1910 is open: (a) is answered (five rungs, then hits), (b) is answered (the
pack extension load), and both answers are measurements, not inferences.
subject: MECHANISM LOCATED (s473x): a warm Moo+`has` run costs ~4.4 s because Sub::Quote calls pack("F",0) at load, which `load`s cl/pcl-pack.lisp from SOURCE every run (= #1202, USER-PARKED) â the fasl ladder DOES settle (five runs) and the eval cache is innocent
